newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower, market awaits bank report.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower, market awaits bank report.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed broadly lower as market sentiment was weighed down by caution ahead of the release of Malaysia's central bank report on Friday, dealers and analysts said.

They said reports that Malaysia has decided to freeze ties with Singapore also gave investors an excuse to sell in the morning. But, the Malaysian government said on Thursday it had not made any decision to suspend ties with the island nation.
"The Bank Negara report is a more significant issue than the row with Singapore," said a foreign brokerage house analyst.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended down 2.28 points at 1,223.31, while the all-share EMAS index closed 1.28 points lower at 358.27.
Analysts said investors would be looking for any hint about Bank Negara's future monetary policy.

They said there has been speculation that the central bank may raise the statutory reserve requirement of banks to mop up excess funds in the banking system. Such a move will keep interest rates firm, analysts said.
"We don't expect surprises. Sentiment should be positive after the report is out," said the foreign firm analyst.
